title: Natembeya joins Sifuna in Dallas as Linda Mwananchi US tour moves to Houston, Seattle and California
key_points: Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya has joined Senator Edwin Sifuna's tour of Kenyan communities in the US.
Natembeya said he arrived in Dallas, Texas, on Friday, according to The Star.
Next stops are Houston, the Seattle area, San Francisco and Oakland, ending in Silicon Valley on December 7.
The team promises Kenyans abroad better consular services and cheaper remittances.
content:
Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya has joined Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna on his tour of Kenyan communities in the United States. The tour is run by Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi movement ahead of the 2027 General Election.

According to The Star, Natembeya announced on social media that he arrived in Dallas, Texas, on Friday, November 27. The Star said Natembeya helps coordinate Sifuna's presidential campaign. The same day, back in Kenya, DAP-K party leader Eugene Wamalwa removed Natembeya as one of the party's deputy leaders, as we reported on Friday.

Where the tour has been

The tour started on November 21 and runs to December 7. Mwakilishi, a diaspora news site, reported these earlier stops:

  • Hackettstown, New Jersey (Nov 21): opening of the movement's first US office.
  • Allentown, Pennsylvania (Nov 22): a church service and a town hall.
  • Maryland and Washington DC (Nov 23–25): a community dinner and meetings with women's, youth and policy groups.

Vihiga Senator Godfrey Osotsi and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza travelled with Sifuna on the first leg, Mwakilishi and Streamline reported.

Where the tour goes next

The published schedule, as reported by Mwakilishi and Capital FM, lists:

  • Houston, Texas (Nov 29): a women's caucus and a town hall.
  • Washington State, Seattle area (Dec 3–4): church services, a gala dinner and a town hall in Federal Way and Renton.
  • San Francisco and Oakland (Dec 5): a town hall in the afternoon and a gala dinner in the evening.
  • Silicon Valley (Dec 7): the closing dinner.

Times and places can change, so check with local organisers before you travel.

What the team is promising

Mwakilishi reported that the movement is promising Kenyans abroad:

  • a fully online, one-stop system for consular services, with clear timelines and tracking;
  • more staff and service points at Kenyan missions, and quick action on fraud reports;
  • lower remittance costs, below 3 percent, by removing taxes and paperwork;
  • a bigger say in government decisions, and wider voting access.

"We want your country to be there for you," Sifuna told diaspora Kenyans, according to Mwakilishi. Sifuna has also said his first rally after returning home will be in Eldoret, Capital FM reported.

The other side

Sifuna's main message is that the current government has neglected Kenyans abroad. The government has not responded to these claims in the reports we read. Earlier this week Sifuna answered critics of the tour, and US filings showed a plan to raise funds from the diaspora, as we reported on Thursday.

What you can do

  • If you want to attend: look for the event details shared by Kenyan community groups in Houston, Seattle or the Bay Area, and confirm the time and venue before you go.
  • Ask your own questions: town halls usually take questions, so prepare one on the issues that matter to you, such as passports, voting or remittances.
  • Check your voter status: diaspora Kenyans can currently vote only in the presidential election. Watch for IEBC announcements on diaspora voter registration before 2027.
  • Hear all sides: other leaders and parties also court the diaspora. Compare their plans before you decide.
